extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: The following policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) guidelines. A provider must make all reasonable efforts to determine whether there is other coverage for an automobile or workplace injury, such as under automobile or workers' compensation insurance, and must promptly report as described below, in claims submitted to Humana, and any such other coverage that is identified. Additionally, a provider must bill a patient's automobile or workplace injury insurance plan, if applicable, before billing the patient's Humana MA plan. Finally, a provider must promptly forward to Humana any determination by an automobile or workplace insurance plan made with respect to a claim for a Humana MA enrollee's injuries. A provider's failure to promptly fulfill any requirement could affect Humana's disposition of a claim after initial receipt and/or after initial adjudication. Humana expects providers to abide by the MSP billing requirements when submitting claims to Humana MA plans. If a provider identifies automobile insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. Humana may deny a claim when payment has been made, or when payment may reasonably be expected to be made, under any applicable liability insurance arrangement, including self-insurance, no-fault insurance or workers' compensation law or plan. reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) guidelines. A provider must make all reasonable efforts to determine whether there is other coverage for an automobile or workplace injury, such as under automobile or workers' compensation insurance, and must promptly report as described below, in claims submitted to Humana, and any such other coverage that is identified. Additionally, a provider must bill a patient's automobile or workplace injury insurance plan, if applicable, before billing the patient's Humana MA plan. Finally, a provider must promptly forward to Humana any determination by an automobile or workplace insurance plan made with respect to a claim for a Humana MA enrollee's injuries. A provider's failure to promptly fulfill any requirement could affect Humana's disposition of a claim after initial receipt and/or after initial adjudication. Humana expects providers to abide by the MSP billing requirements when submitting claims to Humana MA plans. If a provider identifies automobile insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent:

Attach the following to the claim, if available:

Copy of the explanation of benefits (EOB) from the primary insurance carrier

Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier

Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent:

Enter occurrence code 01 or 02, as applicable, and the accident date in fields 33 - 35

Attach the following to the claim, if available:

Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier

Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable If a provider identifies workers' compensation insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent:

Attach the following to the claim, if available:

Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier

Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers' compensation coverage For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent:

Enter condition code 02, 05, or 77, as applicable, in fields 18 - 28

Attach the following to the claim, if available:

Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier

Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers' compensation coverage Note: Medicare benefits are secondary regardless of whether the patient wishes to file a workers' compensation claim. Humana may deny a claim for healthcare services provided due to an automobile or workplace injury if it is submitted without the information above. Humana may deny a claim when payment has been made, or when payment may reasonably be expected to be made, under any applicable liability insurance arrangement, including self-insurance, no-fault insurance or workers' compensation law or plan. Humana may also require providers to pursue and exhaust available no-fault insurance or workers' compensation coverage and to demonstrate reasonable efforts to exhaust any other applicable coverage, before submitting claims to Humana for payment. Note: For more guidance on the MSP provisions and billing requirements, see the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services' MSP booklet and the MSP manual in the References section of this policy.

Humana Medicaid plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable state Medicaid agency requirements.
